report.title: vanityURLs Continuity And Third-Party Operability Audit

headline.statement: vanityURLs has a portable codebase, but canonical continuity and existing-service takeover remain blocked by public evidence gaps in authority, custody, recovery, and independent proof.

subject.name: vanityURLs
subject.description: Community-maintained open-source Cloudflare Workers short-link redirector

businessConcerns.statement: Can a new maintainer take over the canonical project with minimal creator involvement?

conclusion.summary: The code and public decision history are strong, but canonical maintainer appointment, cross-repository authority, administrative controls, release-signer recovery, and successor access are not defined and exercised end to end.

businessConcerns.statement: Can a third party establish and operate a new, independently controlled vanityURLs instance?

conclusion.statement: Plausible, but not yet proven easy
conclusion.summary: The stateless, Git-backed design, MIT license, setup/detach/upgrade tooling, tests, and operator documentation support this outcome. A non-creator has not been observed completing setup, release, deployment, rollback, and recovery with measured assistance.

businessConcerns.statement: Can a third party take over and operate the existing project, v8s.link domain, and demo service?

conclusion.summary: GitHub, Cloudflare, registrar/domain, Terraform state, secrets, deployment, alert, renewal, and recovery custody are external to the repositories and have no evidenced transfer path.

businessConcerns.statement: If the creators abandon the project, can someone else pick it up and evolve it?

conclusion.statement: Yes for a fork, probably with moderate effort; no assurance for canonical continuity
conclusion.summary: Public source, tests, documentation, ADRs, release history, and a low-state runtime provide a credible technical foundation. Preserving the existing identity, trusted releases, domain, and service requires controls not demonstrated here.

included: Repository files and Git history for the four pinned repositories
Public GitHub pull requests, issues, projects, releases, workflows, and Actions metadata
Approved local documentation folders and public website material
excluded: Cloud, registrar, secret, Terraform-state, billing, contract, and private operating records
Dependency restores, tests, builds, Terraform operations, deployments, and recovery exercises
Post-cutoff facts except explicitly labeled validation

limitations.description: Only public, read-only evidence was approved.
limitations.impact: Control transfer for the existing project and demo instance cannot be proved from the available evidence.

limitations.description: No local dependency restore, test, build, deployment, Terraform operation, or recovery exercise was performed.
limitations.impact: Independent operation remains plausible but unproved.

limitations.description: Authenticated ownership, billing, secret custody, live settings, and runtime evidence were not available.
limitations.impact: Canonical continuity and existing-service takeover remain unresolved.
